dossier.public_summary: The dip is not one consistent depth: odd and even dips differ by a factor of ~4 and a secondary dip appears at phase 0.66, both signatures of an eclipsing binary at twice the reported period. Depths vary widely even within the same pipeline and individual transits vary by an order of magnitude, confirming a binary rather than a planet.

reasons.why: Strong odd/even depth difference points to an eclipsing binary at twice the 8.84 d period, not a planet at 8.84 d.
Real secondary eclipse with snr 8.471 well above best_brightening_snr 4.34 and chi2 21.06 vs dof 9 in phase_curve; confirmed as secondary_over_bump 1.952.

Depth changes intrinsically with p_constant 2.054e-15 and p_constant_all 2.054e-15; SPOC p_constant 9.17e-06 alone, transit_depths p_consistent 1.5596e-93 with share_of_top_3 0.799 driven by outliers up to 4137 ppm vs mean 571 ppm.
Independent scorer ranks as strongly non-planet-like, consistent with binary signatures above.
